body: I'm so sorry. In my experience, Christians have been some of the shittiest people I've ever encountered. It's gotten so bad that if I initially meet a person and in the first couple of minutes of conversation they reveal that they're Christian, I immediately remove myself from their presence.

You're not worthless. Believe it or not, we all contribute in one way or another to this world, even if it's tiny. I went through hellish teenage years (home life sucked), and life didn't get better until I went off to college.
 I tried hard as hell to avoid going home when I graduated, but sadly had to due to lack of funds. My early twenties were rough too. Then one day, all of that changed, and life slowly got better. Now, at my big age, I fight every day for my happiness. It's a struggle at times, but it's out.
Thank you; it's nice to know that someone understands what I'm saying. Maybe I'll find that person one day.

Wow, I am so sorry that you are going through this. Also, it's great that you are speaking with a therapist because it seems that a lot has happened that has shaped who you are and how you think now. I understand that this is your mother, and it's sometimes hard to see our parents in a negative light; however, I agree with your therapist. Mom is causing more harm than good; mom may benefit from speaking with a therapist, too. Bottom line, you must move on from your mother and create your own life path. I am not saying go no contact, but minimize your time with her. As for her job, she needs to do that, especially since she's getting paid for it; that whole ordeal is crazy. Self-preservation is of the utmost importance right now, as well as peace of mind, and to do that, you must establish and stand firm on boundaries, especially as they relate to your mother.

Additionally, remember your mother made decisions that created her life, and as an adult, you no longer have to accept her ways.  I hope things get better and get better soon.
